question: Is spec/test/integration-e2e.test.ts deterministic at the base appport@268c9b4 under the T4 regression command?
tree: fresh copy of the prepared fixture (prepare-checkout.sh T4 semantics, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile), no changes
earlierObservation: one preflight regression run at the base failed spec/test/integration-e2e.test.ts (`tickets.list@1 not declared`) while a `pnpm test` run at the base passed fully
conclusion: Not deterministic in general, but passes on a quiet machine (3/3 here). Root cause (from source): spec/test/support/work-order-fixtures.ts freePort() listens on port 0, reads the port and CLOSES the probe before the Python provider binds it; vitest runs test files in parallel, so another file's server can take that port in the gap, and the test then reads a different application's manifest (one that does not declare tickets.list@1). The 5 s start-up wait (100 x 50 ms) is also tight under CPU load (e.g. a local model running).
evaluatorHandling: course-001 lists spec/test/integration-e2e.test.ts in acceptance.regression.knownFlaky: if the regression fails and every failing file is known-flaky, the suite is run once more and the rerun is scored; both runs are recorded as evidence. This mirrors run-acceptance.sh's rerun rule (which in the upstream script only parses cargo output).
